title: Fewest marks
rule: Each figure and object made of the fewest cut shapes that keep the incident readable.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: every figure and object HANDMADE cut paper in code (films/swarm/99-ways/kit/cutpaper99.py: scissor-faceted polygons, flat papers with the LoC 1934 sheet's fibre as relative tone, one down-right paper shadow per piece)

AGENT 5 pieces (trousers, shirt cut in one with both sleeves, waistcoat, head with a nose as its only facial mark, hair) + PENCIL 1; STRANGER 3 (coat, head, hat); CLOCK 3 (face, hour hand, minute hand at 4:10); KEY 3 (hook, key with its bow hole, SERVICE tag); CUPBOARD 2 (dark carcass, door on the left jamb); SERVICE DOOR 2 (door, card); TICKET WINDOW 3 (glass, frame with the pane cut out, sill); MEMO 1; DESK 1

a parts strip across the head of the page: every figure laid out in its separate pieces with its count in the pen hand (agent: 5, pencil: 1, stranger: 3, clock: 3, key: 3, cupboard: 2, SERVICE door: 2, ticket window: 3, memo: 1, desk: 1)
six panels E0-E5 assembled from exactly those pieces; one wall paper and one floor paper per panel as ground

lettering (memo, tag, card, TICKET OFFICE) in the shared pen hand; the four canon lines in the shared cut-paper balloons (penlib.balloon_piece); hand-ruled borders (penlib.border_mask); folio '16 / Fewest marks' (pen99.folio)

the stranger's three pieces are scissored to the window opening (inside the frame, down to the sill's top edge, y = 452 in panel px) with cv2.intersectConvexConvex for the coat and head and a mask cut for the hat, so no paper of hers lies on the office wall

events.E0: panel 1: memo on the desk, clock behind; he rises and turns to go
events.E1: panel 2: walking; the stranger behind the ticket window glass; question balloon tailed to her
events.E2: panel 3: head tipped back to the clock at 4:10; answer balloon tailed to him
events.E3: panel 4: she has turned away and is stepping off past the right jamb, half hidden by the frame; thanks balloon; he walks on
events.E4: panel 5: he holds the cupboard door open on its left jamb; key on its hook with the SERVICE tag
events.E5: panel 6: pencil to his chin, forgetting balloon; key on hook; SERVICE door shut

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the cupboard panel: the agent reaches the closed cupboard (two pieces), the door swings open on its left jamb showing the key's three pieces, then the E5 panel is laid and its balloon added
beat_frames: b01: panels E0-E3 laid; the cupboard panels still empty sheet
b02: E4 panel: the agent arrives at the closed cupboard (carcass + door, 2 pieces)
b03: the cupboard door swings open on its left jamb; the key's 3 pieces (hook, key, tag) show
b04: E5 panel laid: pencil to his chin, no line yet
b05: + the forgetting balloon; key unmoved, SERVICE door shut (= the page)

weaknesses: figures are deliberately schematic (oval heads with a nose as the only facial mark); the agent reads by waistcoat, sleeves and pencil, not by likeness to Rothstein's agent
lettering (memo, tag, SERVICE card, TICKET OFFICE, balloons) is pen hand, not cut shapes, and is not counted in the piece totals; one wall and one floor paper per panel are ground, not counted
the parts strip's small pieces (clock hands, pencil, hook) are tiny at phone width; the counts are lettered beside them

changed: stranger's coat, head and hat cut to the window opening, ending at the sill top in P2-P4 (piece counts unchanged: 3)
P4: she is turned away and moved 128 px toward the right jamb, half behind the frame, leaving
